{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-hi-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"dfe6a7954e3ca347cfe3c325702677185fe9a34a31041f90890c75fa57d7cf9e","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-hi-class-3:lineage:96","source_registry_sha256":"1323c0f691f132d6e9e9a263c68306b972b82c8bbaa5a48a33a79177660764be","source_liveness_sha256":"27cf6d56fae2d5323c61bcbb69f0d992aeceb71a7dae4302b1f14baa17651cb0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Vehicle Registration, Ownership Documents and Title","heading":"C — Vehicle Registration, Ownership Documents and Title","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Vehicle Registration, Ownership Documents and Title

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Hawaii law requires the vehicle you drive on public highways to be registered in the county where you operate it, and to be licensed every year by that same county [A01].
Why it matters: registration is county-based, not state-based, which surprises many newcomers.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
A vehicle must have a current, valid safety inspection certificate before it can be registered, with proof of motor vehicle insurance required for cars, buses and trucks at inspection and proof of liability coverage required for motorcycles [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Registration creates the official record of a vehicle's ownership, and when a vehicle is first registered in Hawaii it is inspected and weighed so that its identification number and its weight are properly recorded [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Registrations and titles are issued by the appropriate agency in each county, and the Hawaii certificate of ownership, the title, is held by the legal owner or by the lien holder until the loan on the vehicle is paid off [A01].
Why it matters: the lien holder keeps the title while a loan is outstanding; the driver keeps only the registration.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
The registration certificate is issued to the purchaser, who must keep it in the vehicle, and registrations are staggered so that each one expires annually at the end of its twelfth month [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
Registration renewal applications are mailed to your last recorded address, and any error you find on the application should be reported promptly to the county agency [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
To renew by mail you send both parts of the renewal application, without detaching the stub, with a check or money order for the exact total fee shown, mailed to your county agency within ten working days before the end of the expiration month [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
A vehicle currently registered in Hawaii may have its registration renewed online through the state motor vehicle renewal site by selecting the county of registration [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A02
When a registered owner's address changes from the one on the registration application, the owner must notify the county agency in writing within thirty days, giving the old and new addresses, the vehicle license number, the make and the vehicle identification number [A02].
Why it matters: the registration address change is a written notice, like the driver license address change.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A02
When a registered owner's name changes from the one on the certificate of ownership, the owner must appear in person at the county agency within thirty days with proof of the name change, the properly endorsed certificate of ownership and the current year's registration certificate [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A02
A member of the United States armed forces on duty at a military installation in Hawaii who is a legal resident of another state may keep the vehicle registered in that state and is exempt from the Hawaii excise tax on vehicles brought in, the county and state weight taxes, the state registration fee and the highway beautification fee [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A02
A veteran who is one hundred percent medically disabled and presents the accompanying paperwork is exempt from paying registration fees [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A02
A service member whose vehicle was last registered and titled in another state and is now subject to Hawaii registration must give the county agency where stationed an application, the out-of-state title and registration, a current Hawaii safety inspection certificate, a shipping receipt and a verification of the vehicle identification number [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A02
For a vehicle from a non-title state, the application is accompanied by the registration certificate, one or more notarized bills of sale establishing the chain of ownership, a current Hawaii safety inspection and a verification of the vehicle serial number [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A02
When you buy a new vehicle in Hawaii you must obtain an application form countersigned by the licensed new car dealer certifying the sale [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
For a new vehicle bought in another state, where ownership documents vary, Hawaii accepts either the manufacturer's certificate of origin or a notarized bill of sale [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
A new vehicle bought in a foreign country needs a bill of sale from the foreign dealer issued in your name, a manufacturer's certification label showing compliance with United States standards, and a seventeen-character vehicle identification number [A02].
Why it matters: the seventeen-character identification number is the detail that trips up imported vehicles.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A02
A used vehicle bought in a foreign country must come with a certificate of registration and a bill of sale as proof of ownership [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A03
When you buy a used vehicle in another state, the seller named on that state's title must give you the title itself, the registration certificate and a notarized bill of sale [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A03
A used vehicle from a non-title state comes with that state's current registration certificate or certification of registration plus two notarized bills of sale, the first covering the previous owner's sale to the seller and the second covering the seller's sale to you [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A03
A vehicle still registered in another state may receive a Hawaii permit, a temporary registration, that allows driving on Hawaii roads until the home registration expires, but never for longer than a twelve-month period [A03].
Why it matters: twelve months is the hard ceiling on the temporary permit, whatever the home registration says.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A03
To get the temporary permit you must present the vehicle's certificate of registration, its shipping receipt and a current Hawaii safety inspection certificate [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A03
When the temporary permit expires you must register the vehicle with the county agency where you reside, unless you are a member of the United States armed forces [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A03
Motorcycles, trailers and semi-trailers display one license plate on the rear, while every other vehicle must display a plate on both the front and the rear [A03].
Why it matters: the front plate rule is a common test question for car drivers.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A03
Mopeds must be inspected, registered and licensed, and the moped's license plate and inspection sticker must be displayed on its rear [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0023]

Misconceptions: the title is held by the lien holder while a loan is outstanding, not by the driver; the registration certificate, not the title, must stay in the vehicle; registration is renewed yearly with the county, not the state; a registration address change is a written notice while a registration name change requires a personal visit; the temporary permit for an out-of-state vehicle can never exceed twelve months even if the home registration runs longer.

Mnemonics: Register with the county, renew every twelfth month, report a change within thirty days; two plates on a car, one on a motorcycle, trailer or moped; a permit for an out-of-state car lasts at most a year.

Glossary: certificate of ownership (the Hawaii vehicle title); lien holder (the lender who holds the title until the loan is paid); staggered registration (expirations spread across the year, each at the end of a twelfth month); manufacturer's certificate of origin (the ownership document for a new vehicle before its first title); non-title state (a state that issues registrations but no titles); temporary registration permit (the Hawaii permit for a vehicle still registered elsewhere).

Dynamic facts: the online renewal web address can change and is not stated as stable knowledge; fee amounts are not printed on these pages; registration periods, document lists and display rules are stable statutory facts of this printing.
